summary: The main article describes a visible light-mediated 3-component carbosulfonylation of alkynes using carboxylic acids and arylsulfinates. It includes a table for reaction optimization, two schemes detailing the substrate scope and synthetic applications, and a mechanistic proposal involving dual photocatalytic cycles.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Approaches to Carbosulfonylation of Alkynes
items.description: Compares previous literature methods for carbosulfonylation using nickel catalysis or redox-active esters with the current metal-free work.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of Reaction Conditions a
items.description: Lists the screening of solvents, photocatalysts, and additives to optimize the yield and diastereoselectivity of the 3-component reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Reaction Scope
items.description: Displays the broad substrate scope for alkynes, carboxylic acids, and sulfinates, including late-stage functionalization of bioactive molecules.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Application to the Synthesis of Sedum Alkaloids
items.description: Demonstrates the utility of the method by synthesizing pyrrolallosedamine and pyrrolsedamine.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Mechanistic Studies
items.description: Shows control experiments including radical quenching with TEMPO and the reaction of proposed intermediates.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Plausible Mechanistic Proposal (PC = 4CzIPN)
items.description: Illustrates the proposed dual photocatalytic cycles for the generation of sulfinyl and alkyl radicals.
